correctness.rationale: Under independent sites and Poisson counts the failure probability is the product of Laplace transforms. The negative log transform has strictly negative second derivative at t>0 by nondegeneracy and tilted variance, extends strictly concavely to zero, and gives the unique balanced allocation. For a real count x the exponent's derivative is -h((H+c)/x-c), with h(t)=(t+c)φ'(t)-φ(t), h(0)>0 and h strictly decreasing. Subtract λ0t to obtain ψ(t)=o(t). For q>0, ψ tends to -log q and integrability of its decreasing derivative gives tψ'(t)→0. For q=0, ψ diverges: if the nondecreasing gap ψ-tψ' were bounded, integrating (ψ/t)' from t to infinity would bound ψ, a contradiction. These limits prove the exact one-site criterion including strict finite-time optimality at equality and the λ0=0 and q=0 cases. Otherwise the unique root gives the continuous target. Adjacent feasible integer differences are negative at their feasibility endpoints, strictly increasing in H by strict decrease of φ', and eventually positive. At a tie strict concavity and the mean-value theorem put the continuous target strictly between the two counts, giving disjoint ordered threshold brackets, no skipped counts, and the count asymptotic. The two-rate example was separately recomputed and matches the stated dwell and detection probabilities. value.rationale: The exact contrast between a positive rate floor with an atom and the same floor without one resolves when a fixed overhead can suppress rotation for all horizons. Combined with the discrete thresholds it describes both a qualitative experimental-design boundary and the order and location of all changes in optimal effort. The result is about the idealized iid at-least-one objective, not empirical model validity or detection-rate estimation.
